Our purpose

Mission of the project

How would you describe the mission of this project to a friend?

A brief history

A realistic VR equestrian simulator designed to help children with autism safely experience the joy of riding, caring for horses, and building confidence. Through gentle activities and rewarding challenges, the game encourages confidence, coordination, independence, and emotional connection.

Expected impact

Why Equielle matters

i

Therapeutic

A calming, structured VR experience that supports children with autism in emotional regulation.

ii

Educational

Teaches basic horse care and riding routines, step by step, in the order they happen at a real barn.

iii

Social

Makes equestrian therapy more widely accessible, without needing a live horse.

Inside the game

Four steps of every ride

Equielle moves at the rider's pace, from the first brush stroke to the last ribbon. Hover or tap a card to see how each step works in VR.

  • Step 01

    Care

    Groom, feed, and get your horse ready for the day.

    See it in VR
    01

    Care, in VR

    • Reach out and brush along the coat. The controller hums where the horse likes it most.
    • Fill the hay net and water bucket before every session.
    • There is no rush. The horse waits for you.
    Gentle, seated play
  • Step 02

    Bond

    Build trust through calm, gentle interaction.

    See it in VR
    02

    Bond, in VR

    • Hold your hand still and let the horse choose to come to you.
    • Your voice and your breathing set the pace. There is no rush.
    • Trust only ever grows. Nothing you do can lose it.
    Self-paced · no fail state
  • Step 03

    Ride

    Learn to steer, balance, and jump in VR.

    See it in VR
    03

    Ride, in VR

    • Walk, trot, and canter using head tilt or a single hand.
    • A guided line lights up the path to each jump.
    • Comfort settings: seated mode, snap turning, softened motion.
    Seated or standing
  • Step 04

    Grow

    Earn ribbons, unlock rewards, and gain confidence.

    See it in VR
    04

    Grow, in VR

    • A ribbon for every session, not just for clear rounds.
    • Unlock new tack, new arenas, and a second horse to care for.
    • A progress wall you can show the people at home.
    Progress you keep

The Equielle way

A patient horse, a quiet barn, and all the time in the world.

Riders go at their own pace, with no rush to finish. A timer runs quietly in the background, so each time they practise or compete they can try to beat their own best.

  • Ride at your own pace
  • No rush to finish
  • Beat your best time
  • No fail states
  • Seated or standing
  • Gentle motion

Development

How it's built

Equielle began as primitive shapes in Unity and grew into a full stable yard, one area at a time.

i

Greyboxed level design

The barn, grooming station and arena were blocked out with simple shapes first, so the layout and flow could be tested before any detail was added.

ii

Hands-on interaction

Players use their own hands in VR to reach, brush and feed. The challenge was turning real-life movement into motion that feels natural and calm.

iii

A horse that moves on its own

The horse finds its way around the yard with Unity's AI Navigation, walking on a baked NavMesh instead of fixed paths.

iv

Designed for comfort

Riders set their own pace, there is no game-over screen, and seated play keeps every session low pressure. The timer is only there so they can try to beat their own best.

  • Unity
  • C#
  • Unity XR
  • AI Navigation
  • Low-poly 3D

Start to finish

Development timeline

  1. Stage 1

    Core mechanics and game flow

    Defined the game from start to finish and drafted the flow with drawings and pictures.

  2. Stage 2

    Greybox the level

    Blocked out the barn, yard and arena, and laid out the assets needed for level 1.

  3. Stage 3

    First gameplay loop

    Built the first section to play start to finish: gathering gear, cleaning and tacking the horse.

  4. Stage 4

    Playable prototype

    Refined the loop and tested it until it ran smoothly, then showcased it.

  5. Stage 5

    Riding and rewards

    Added the jump course, ribbons, new tack and arenas, and a second horse to care for.

The creator

Biography

Meet Ella

and her horse, Lucky

Ella Yang is a high school student at the Orange County School of the Arts (OCSA), where she studies in the Instrumental Music Conservatory's Strings program. Outside of school, she is a dedicated equestrian who trains with her horse, Lucky, and competes in showjumping events. Combining her love of horses with her interest in technology, Ella created this passion project to make the joy and connection of horseback riding more accessible to children with autism.

  • Discipline · Showjumping
  • Studies · Strings, OCSA
  • Builds in · Unity & VR
